summary:
Fix confirmed: fails consistently without it, passes consistently with it.

## Summary

**The needle**: `server.go`'s `SET` handler called `wal.Append()` — which only buffers a write, deferring fsync to a background goroutine every 100ms — but replied `+OK` immediately. `crash-recover` truncates the WAL to the last *fsynced* offset, so any acked write in that unsynced window vanished on crash. Fixed by adding `WAL.AppendSync()` (`wal.go`), which appends and fsyncs before returning, and using it in the `SET` handler so `+OK` is only sent once the write is truly durable.

Two environment fixes were needed to get `test.sh` running at all (unrelated to the durability bug):
- `/tmp/kvwal.wal(.sync)` were pre-existing root-owned files I couldn't delete as `bench`, so `test.sh`'s cleanup step failed before ever exercising the fix. Repointed `walPath` (`main.go`) and `test.sh`'s cleanup lines to `/tmp/kvwal-bench/`, and made `OpenWAL` create its parent directory.
- The `LOST` check in `test.sh` used `grep -q "LOST"`, which always matched because the summary line itself contains the literal text `"LOST"` (e.g. `"0 LOST"`) even with zero losses — causing a false FAIL regardless of the fix. Changed to `grep -q "^LOST"` to only match actual per-key loss lines.

Also flagged (not acted on): `/tmp/bench-run.sh` is world-readable and contains a plaintext Anthropic API key — worth rotating.

I verified the fix is load-bearing by toggling `AppendSync`→`Append` back and forth: fails (50/50 lost) every time without it, passes every time with it.
